headline: API Reports U.S. Crude Oil and Gasoline Inventory Builds
summary: The American Petroleum Institute estimated that U.S. crude oil inventories increased by 5.3 million barrels in the week ending November 13, following a 9 million barrel rise in the prior week.
why: Crude oil inventory reports from the American Petroleum Institute serve as a closely watched precursor to official government data, helping investors gauge supply and demand balances in the global petroleum market.

impacts.name: WTI crude oil
impacts.why: Rising crude oil inventories typically indicate weaker demand or higher supply, exerting downward pressure on oil prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Unexpected builds in domestic crude inventories signal potential oversupply, prompting downward price adjustments in the energy market.
